sourceAnchors.visualArbitrationNote: Printed page 459 states the general experimental mark of the neurosis chapter as a `Diskrepanz zwischen Rand und Mitte`: Rand (vital Sexual- and Kontakttriebe) often shows source-described immature/infantile reactions, whereas Mitte shows `überreife`, often `übernormale` censorship reactions. The canonical derivative corrupts `Mitte` as `Mit/e`; the PDF governs the term.

sourceExcerpt: Auf Grund der Ergebnisse von mehreren hundert Triebanalysen an Neurotikern fanden wir als das besondere Merkzeichen für Neurose die Diskrepanz Zwischen Rand und Mit/e.
romanianRendering: Szondi formulează drept marcaj experimental general al nevrozelor o discrepanță Rand–Mitte: la Rand apar frecvent reacții pe care el le numește imature/infantile în domeniile sexual și de contact, iar în Mitte reacții de cenzură `überreif` sau `übernormal`.
doctrinalStatement: În syndromatica istorică a nevrozelor, Szondi pune în centru o `Diskrepanz zwischen Rand und Mitte`: Rand-ul vital (S și C, descris aici prin Sexual- și Kontakttriebe) tinde să poarte reacții `unreif/infantil`, în timp ce Mitte este caracterizată prin cenzuri `überreif/übernormal`. Aceasta este o relație structurală între Rand și Mitte, nu o trăsătură globală a persoanei și nu un diagnostic contemporan.
conditions: Interpret the source claim at the Rand/Mitte relation level rather than from one isolated factor reaction.
Preserve the historical meanings of `unreif`, `überreif` and `übernormal` as source terminology.
exceptions: Do not infer a contemporary neurosis or other diagnosis from one immature Rand reaction or one strict Mitte reaction.
Do not translate `unreif/überreif` into a generic developmental or moral judgment about the person.
Do not infer sexual biography or contact behavior from the structural Rand description alone.
scopeNotes: The detailed sexual and contact reaction lists on page 459 remain source atlas material at this compaction level.
This record captures the general common marker before the source differentiates specific Mitte defenses and neurosis forms.
ambiguities: Canonical U005122 renders `Mitte` as `Mit/e`; admitted PDF printed page 459 resolves the term.
